terms.gloss: a dugout or small boat; here, an outrigger canoe
evidence: Plin. NH 6.105: monoxylīs lintribus, of the dugouts that bring pepper down to the ports of India
terms.comment: The classical word for a small boat hollowed from a trunk, which Pliny uses of the boats of the Indian coast. No ancient source has the outrigger itself, the floats on booms at the sides; the word for the whole boat is the classical one used of a modern thing, and ours. The booms can be described: trabēs utrimque ēminentēs, a description of ours (see the examples).

phrases.latin: ex quā piper monoxylīs lintribus … convehunt
phrases.english: from which they bring pepper down … in dugouts made from a single trunk
and the cargoes are brought out and carried off in small boats

phrases.latin: Ecce piscātōrēs lintrem in lītus subdūcunt.
phrases.english: Look, the fishermen are hauling their canoe up the beach.

phrases.latin: Trabēs utrimque ēminentēs lintrem stabiliunt, nē ēvertātur.
phrases.english: The booms sticking out on both sides keep the canoe steady, so that it doesn’t capsize.

sources: Lewis & Short: linter · Lewis & Short: monoxylus
